newsitem.title: UK: Traders and refiners diverge in Med Urals market.
newsitem.headline: Traders and refiners diverge in Med Urals market.

text.p: The Urals crude market in the Mediterranean was schizophrenic on Friday with trader to trader business talked at levels above what end-user purchasers would pay.
Given the relative scarcity of Russian barrels and the supposed healthy demand sparked by strong refinery margins, traders were able to talk values up to around dated Brent -$1.00 or -$1.05 a barrel.
"If you can hold on and not buy until July and everything is alright with Kirkuk (Iraqi) deliveries then prices should come off sharply," said one Urals buyer.
Most west Mediterranean refiners were said to be covered for the remainder of June and trader activity centred on short covering into the eastern Med, traders said
One refinery operator envisaged doing a balancing deal at around dated Brent -$1.10, a number he believed closer to real market value.

Higher Ural numbers were pushing some buyers towards the plentiful supply of West African barrels, with one Spanish major believed to have picked up cheaply a distressed sandwich Bonny light/medium two days ago.
With the arbitrage window to Asia reopened Far Eastern buyers have taken more than 200,000 barrels per day off the spot market in the latter part of the week.
But their focus on heavier sours has left Nigerian material still sweating for buyers.

A British major bought a million-barrel Bonny light/medium sandwich loading 22-23 June yesterday at dated Brent +25 cents/flat. The cheap numbers meant other deals were getting done confidentially, one trader said.

Two promptish Qua Iboes were heard distressed and attracting little interest. Their notional bid/offer range was about dated +10/+20 cts, sharply lower than the deals down mid-week at +26 and +23 cents.
